Localisation of industries means concentrating industries in one area. The area with the industries grows, but other areas lose investment and jobs, so structural unemployment can be created in the neglected regions.

Reducing production costs, encouraging skilled labour and encouraging subsidiary industries are advantages of localisation, not disadvantages.

question: When combination of two goods which a consumer derive equal satisfaction is plotted on a graph, the graph is known as
solution:
An indifference curve shows the different combinations of two goods that give a consumer the same level of satisfaction. The consumer is indifferent between any two points on the same curve.

A demand curve relates price and quantity, a utility curve shows total or marginal utility, and an opportunity curve is not a standard tool of consumer theory.

question: If the population of a school is 600 and 60% are In JSS, how many students are in SSS?
solution:
The school has 600 students, and 60% are in JSS. The number in JSS is:

60100×600=360

The rest are in SSS: 600−360=240. So there are 240 students in SSS.
category: Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis

question: Which of the following NOT among the objectives of OPEC?

option.a: to stabilize the price of oil in the world market
option.b: to established petroleum refineries in all member state
option.c: to stabilize the revenue from oil to producing countries
option.d: to make sure that oil flows to all the consuming countries

solution:
OPEC aims to stabilise world oil prices, stabilise the oil revenue of producing countries and ensure a regular supply of oil to consuming countries.

Establishing petroleum refineries in all member states is not an OPEC objective. Refining is a national industrial decision, and many member states do not have refineries of their own.

question: Which of the following is NOT a function of marketing boards in Nigeria?

option.c: Fixing of prices for farm produce

solution:
Marketing boards were set up to grade farm produce, fix producer prices and market (buy and sell) export crops such as cocoa, palm produce and groundnuts.

Importation of farm produce was not their function; they were concerned with the marketing of domestically produced export crops, not with importing food.

question: Which of the following is NOT included in-measuring the National income through the income approach?

option.b: Profit earned by Nigerian bottling company plc
option.d: Allowance given to an aged mother by a civil servant

solution:
When national income is measured by the income approach, only income earned from producing goods and services is counted: profits, wages, rents and interest.

An allowance given to an aged mother by a civil servant is a transfer payment. It is not payment for any productive activity, so it is not included in national income. Profits of companies and a bricklayer's income are earned from production.

question: A market situation with few sellers and many buyers is called
solution:
A market with a few sellers and many buyers is an oligopoly. Each seller is large enough to affect the market price and must watch the reactions of rivals.

A duopoly has exactly two sellers, a monopoly has one seller, and perfect competition has many sellers as well as many buyers.

question: Which of the following is NOT associated with minimum price legislation?
solution:
Minimum price legislation fixes a price above the equilibrium price to protect producers. At that higher price, producers supply more than consumers are willing to buy, so excess supply (a surplus) occurs.

Excess demand happens when a maximum price is fixed below equilibrium. Wastage of resources and unemployment can also follow minimum price laws, so excess demand is the item not associated with them.

question: The following are problems of development planning in Nigeria EXCEPT
solution:
Development planning in Nigeria has been hindered by inadequate capital, inadequate statistical data and poor implementation of plans.

Under-population is not one of the problems. Nigeria is in fact a populous country, and a larger population can provide more workers and a bigger market.

question: Which of the following is the correct order in the chain of distribution?
solution:
Goods normally move from the producer to the wholesaler, then to the retailer, and finally to the consumer. Each stage adds convenience and moves the goods closer to the final buyer.

The other options put the consumer or retailer before the producer, which reverses the real order.

question: The following determine the level of consumption EXCEPT
solution:
The level of consumption depends mainly on the level of income, the rate of taxes (which reduces disposable income) and savings habits (since income is either consumed or saved).

The political climate may affect confidence, but it is not a direct determinant of how much households consume in the theory of the consumption function.

question: The willingness of an individual backed up with purchasing power at a given time is
solution:
Effective demand is the willingness to buy a good backed by the ability (purchasing power) to pay at a given time. Desire alone is not demand.

Demand in general includes ability to pay, but the precise term for willingness plus purchasing power is effective demand. Desire is only a wish, and utility is satisfaction.

question: In income determination theory, acceleration principles shows that

option.a: investment is the causes, while income is the effects
option.b: income and investment are both effects
option.c: incomes is of on effect on investment
option.d: income and investment are both causes

solution:
The acceleration principle links investment to changes in income: when income rises, firms need more capital equipment, so investment increases. In the simple statement used here, investment is treated as the initiating cause and income as the effect, and the higher income then induces further investment.

The other options either make both variables effects or make both causes, which does not capture the accelerator relationship.

question: A major characteristics of a firm operating at a long-run equilibrium position is that

option.d: fixed cost can not be changed

solution:
In the long run, a firm can change all its inputs: it can build a bigger factory, buy more machines or reduce its scale. There are no fixed costs in the long run because all costs can be varied.

Fixed costs and variable costs are short-run distinctions, so the other options describe the short run.

question: When an economy is having a balance of payment surplus the best alternative opened to it is to
solution:
A balance of payments surplus means the country is receiving more foreign currency than it is paying out. The extra foreign money increases the country's foreign reserves, which strengthens its ability to pay for imports and settle debts.

Devaluing the currency or borrowing abroad would be responses to a deficit, not a surplus. Promoting imports could reduce a surplus, but the direct and safest result of a surplus is a rise in reserves.

question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of capitalism?
solution:
Capitalism is built on free enterprise, private ownership of property and competition, with markets rather than government deciding what to produce.

Detailed economic planning is a feature of a command or socialist economy, where the state directs production. It is not a feature of capitalism.

question: Which of the following is NOT an objective of Economic planning?
solution:
Economic planning aims to allocate resources equitably, achieve economic growth and create employment, among other goals.

Widening the income gap is the opposite of a planning objective. Planners try to reduce inequality, not increase it.

question: The satisfaction derived from the consumption of a commodity is referred to as
solution:
Utility is the satisfaction a consumer derives from consuming a commodity. It is the usefulness or pleasure the good gives to the person who consumes it.

Consumption is the act of using the good, production is making it, and demand is the desire backed by ability to pay.

question: If the standard deviation of a set of numbers is 3.6, what is the variance?
solution:
The variance is the square of the standard deviation:

Variance=(standard deviation)2=3.62=12.96

So the variance is 12.96.
category: Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis

question: Which of the following will NOT bring about an increase in Labour force?
solution:
The labour force is made up of people who are able and willing to work. A fall in the death rate, better medical services and immigration all add to it.

Emigration is the movement of people out of a country. It removes workers from the population, so it does not increase the labour force.

question: The trade-off between two commodities along the Production Possibility Curve (PPC) shows
solution:
Along a production possibility curve, producing more of one good means producing less of the other. The amount of the second good given up is the opportunity cost of the first.

The curve also shows scarcity and unattainable combinations, but the specific trade-off between the two goods illustrates the opportunity cost principle.

question: A price floor is usually fixed

option.a: above the equilibrium and causes surpluses
option.b: below the equilibrium and causes surpluses
option.c: above the equilibrium and causes shortage
option.d: at the equilibrium and causes no shortage

solution:
A price floor (minimum price) is fixed above the equilibrium price. At this higher price, sellers are willing to supply more than buyers want to buy, so a surplus (excess supply) results.

A price fixed below equilibrium would cause a shortage, and a price at equilibrium would cause neither.

question: Economics problems arise in all societies because

option.a: the services of economists are not employed
option.b: resource are not in adequate supply

solution:
Economic problems arise in every society because resources are not available in adequate supply relative to wants. This is the problem of scarcity, and it exists in rich and poor countries alike.

Poor planning, mismanagement and the number of economists may affect how well an economy performs, but they are not the fundamental reason why economic problems exist.

question: Holding money to take care of contingencies is
solution:
People hold money for three main reasons: to buy goods and services (transactions motive), to take advantage of future price changes (speculative motive), and to meet unexpected emergencies (precautionary motive).

Holding money to take care of contingencies — sudden illness, accidents or urgent repairs — is therefore the precautionary motive.

question: The following will occur when maximum price is fixed below the free market price EXCEPT that
solution:
A maximum price fixed below the free-market price makes the good cheaper, so buyers demand more while sellers supply less. This creates excess demand (a shortage), which encourages black markets and rationing.

Excess supply will not occur; excess supply is the result of a minimum price fixed above equilibrium.

question: The problem of "how to produce" in any economy is solved by

option.a: combining capital and labour intensive methods of production
option.b: adopting the least cost method of production
option.c: using capital intensive method of production
option.d: employing the services of a manager

solution:
The “how to produce” problem asks which combination of resources and techniques should be used. The rational answer is to choose the method that produces the desired output at the least cost.

Capital-intensive or labour-intensive methods are only examples of techniques; the manager must compare their costs and pick the cheapest suitable one.

question: If government in a fiscal year has its revenue receipts less than the expenditure, such country is having
solution:
When the government's revenue receipts are less than its expenditure, it is spending more than it earns. This is a deficit budget.

A surplus budget is the opposite, and a balanced budget means revenue equals expenditure.

question: The following are the objectives of agricultural policies in Nigeria EXCEPT

option.a: provision of agricultural raw materials to industrial sectors

solution:
Agricultural policies in Nigeria aim to provide food, supply raw materials to industries and create rural employment, among other goals.

Increasing the prices of agricultural inputs is not an objective. Higher input prices raise farmers' costs and discourage production, so policies usually aim to make inputs cheaper and easier to obtain.

question: The act of cultivating land and rearing of animal for man's use is
solution:
Agriculture is the act of cultivating land and rearing animals for human use. It covers crop farming, livestock, fisheries and forestry.

Forestry and horticulture are branches of agriculture, while monoculture is the growing of a single crop, so none of them is the general term.

question: The revolution of Cassava from ordinary food crop to export crop will lead to

option.a: increase in production of other crops
option.b: increase in the prices of cassava products
option.c: decrease in production of local starch

solution:
When cassava is transformed from an ordinary food crop into an export crop, demand for it rises beyond local consumption. Producers may also use it for starch, flour and other products.

The extra demand pushes up the price of cassava products. It would encourage more cassava production rather than less, and it does not directly increase the production of other crops.

question: MPC + MPS equals
solution:
Every extra naira of income is either consumed or saved, so the marginal propensity to consume (MPC) plus the marginal propensity to save (MPS) must account for the whole addition:

MPC+MPS=1

For example, if a person spends 0.8 of extra income and saves 0.2, the two add up to 1.

question:
A producer who can only influence the price of his product but canNOT determine the quantity to be sold is referred to
as
solution:
A monopolist is the single seller in a market and can influence the price of the product. However, the monopolist cannot force consumers to buy a particular quantity: the quantity sold is decided by buyers' demand at the price chosen.

A monopsonist is a single buyer, and duopoly and oligopoly involve more than one seller.

question: The demand for factors of production is said to be
solution:
The demand for factors of production (land, labour, capital) is a derived demand. Firms do not want these factors for their own sake; they want them because of the goods and services the factors help to produce.

If the demand for the final product rises, the demand for the factors used to make it also rises. Joint, complementary and composite demand describe other relationships between goods.
category: Factors of Production and their Theories

question: A budget is balanced when expected total revenue is
solution:
A budget is balanced when the government's expected total revenue is equal to its expected total expenditure. It plans to spend exactly what it expects to receive.

If revenue is less than expenditure the budget is in deficit, and if revenue is greater it is in surplus.

question: A country is described as developing if

option.c: the income per head is low
option.d: the contribution of tertiary sector to national income is high

solution:
A country is described as developing when income per head is low, along with other features such as high poverty, low industrialisation and poor infrastructure.

Low labour supply, a falling population and a large service sector are not the defining features of a developing country.

question: A country's balance of payments is in deficit when

option.a: a country's payments for imports of invisible goods are greater than her receipts from exports of invisible goods
option.b: the total receipts from her export of visible and invisible goods are greater than her payments for visible and invisible imports
option.c: the total payments for visible and invisible imports are greater than the total receipts from her exports of visible and invisible goods
option.d: It can record a surplus on current account of her balance of payments accounts

solution:
A balance of payments deficit occurs when the country's total payments for visible and invisible imports are greater than its total receipts from visible and invisible exports. The country is spending more foreign exchange than it earns.

A surplus is the opposite, and a deficit on the invisible account alone does not necessarily make the whole balance of payments negative.

question: A firm will shut down in the long run if its earning is
solution:
In the long run, a firm must earn at least normal profit to stay in business. Normal profit is the minimum return needed to keep the entrepreneur in the industry.

If earnings fall below normal profit, the firm cannot cover all its costs (including the opportunity cost of capital), so it will shut down. Super-normal profit is extra profit above normal profit.

question: A firm's average cost decreases in the long-run because of
solution:
In the long run, a firm can expand all its inputs. As it grows, it enjoys increasing returns to scale: output rises proportionately faster than costs, so average cost falls.

Diminishing returns and decreasing average fixed cost are short-run ideas, and diminishing average returns would raise average cost, not lower it.

question: A rise in government expenditure can lead to

option.d: lower importation of raw materials by industries

solution:
A rise in government expenditure injects more money into the economy and increases aggregate demand. If the economy is already near full capacity, this extra demand pulls prices up, so it can lead to higher inflation.

It is more likely to reduce unemployment and raise profits, not increase unemployment or reduce imports of raw materials.

question: A stock exchange is a market that

option.a: deals with the exchange of commodities
option.b: deals with purchase and sales of securities
option.d: exchanges treasury bills for bills of exchange

solution:
A stock exchange is a market where existing securities — shares, bonds and debentures — are bought and sold. It provides a place for investors to trade and for companies to raise capital.

It does not deal in ordinary commodities, stockfish or a direct exchange of treasury bills for bills of exchange.

question: Acceptability , durability, homogeneity , and portability are all attributes of good
solution:
For a commodity to serve as money it should be generally acceptable, durable, homogeneous (every unit the same) and portable (easy to carry).

These are qualities of money, not of markets, government or banks.

question: An agricultural production process which uses more machinery relative to labour is referred to as
solution:
When a farm uses more machinery relative to labour, it is practising capital-intensive farming. Capital (tractors, harvesters, irrigation equipment) replaces human and animal labour.

Land-intensive farming uses more land, large-scale farming describes size, and commercial farming describes production for sale.

question: An argument for the use of commercial policy rest on the need to

option.b: encourage the importation of non-essential goods
option.c: make a country enjoy absolute advantage in production of all goods

solution:
Commercial policy includes tariffs, quotas and other trade measures. One argument for using it is to protect domestic industries from foreign competition, so that they can expand and reduce domestic unemployment.

It is not meant to make imports cheaper, encourage non-essential imports or help a country produce every good at an absolute advantage.

question: An entrepreneur is encouraged to adopt division of labour in production because it

option.a: leads to increased cost of production and lower output
option.c: brings about equal cost and employment opportunities
option.d: leads to increased output and lower cost of production

solution:
Division of labour means breaking production into small tasks performed by different specialised workers. Each worker becomes skilled at one task, time is saved and machines can be used efficiently.

The result is increased output at a lower cost of production, which is why entrepreneurs adopt it. It does not raise costs or lower output.

question: An indication that there is inflation in a country is that

option.a: there is a decrease in the demand for goods and services
option.b: people prefer to lend than to borrow
option.c: the same amount of money buys lower quantity of goods
option.d: there are too many goods in circulation

solution:
The clearest sign of inflation is that the same amount of money buys a smaller quantity of goods. Money is losing purchasing power because prices are rising.

People would rather borrow than lend during inflation (since debts lose real value), and there are not “too many goods” — the problem is too much money chasing too few goods.

question: Another term for equilibrium price is
solution:
The equilibrium price is also called the market clearing price, because at that price the quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied and the market is cleared.

Demand price is the price buyers are willing to pay, a satisfactory price is not a technical term, and a price floor is a minimum price set by government.

question: Cheques are not money because?

option.a: Their use is confined to business hours
option.b: They are not generally acceptable as a medium of exchange
option.c: There are few banks in the rural areas
option.d: They are not issued by the government

solution:
Cheques are not money because they are not generally acceptable as a medium of exchange. A shopkeeper or creditor may refuse a cheque, and it is only an instruction to a bank to pay from the drawer's account.

They are also not legal tender, but the option given here correctly states the general-acceptability reason.

question: Cost push inflation is caused by a

option.a: decrease in the cost of production
option.d: rise in the cost of production

solution:
Cost-push inflation is caused by a rise in the cost of production. When wages, raw materials, fuel or transport become more expensive, producers raise prices to protect their margins.

A decrease in production or transport costs would lower prices, and a rise in demand causes demand-pull inflation, not cost-push.

question: Development plans in West Africa tend to deviate from their targets mainly due to
solution:
Development plans in West Africa often fail to meet their targets mainly because of political instability: coups, changes of government and civil conflicts interrupt projects and cause policies to be abandoned.

Low education, rapid population growth and shortages of manpower create difficulties, but political instability is the major cause of plans being derailed.

question: Economic problems arise mainly as a result of?

option.a: Lack of foresight on the part of resource users
option.b: Inaccurate statistical data in West Africa

solution:
Economic problems arise mainly because of limitations in the availability of resources. Resources are scarce relative to unlimited wants, so choices must be made.

Poor foresight, inaccurate statistics and waste make problems worse, but they are not the fundamental cause.

question: Harmonised monetary and fiscal policies is a feature of
solution:
An economic union goes beyond a common market: member countries also harmonise their monetary and fiscal policies, and may adopt a common currency and common economic institutions.

A free trade area, customs union and common market remove trade barriers but do not require harmonised monetary and fiscal policies.

question: If 20% rise in the price of Whisky leads to a 30% increase in quantity demanded of Schnapps, the cross elasticity of demand is
solution:
Cross elasticity of demand measures how the quantity demanded of one good responds to a change in the price of another:

Exy=% change in quantity of Schnapps% change in price of Whisky=3020=1.5

The positive sign shows that the goods are substitutes.

question: If an increase in the price of crude oil led to an increase in the prices of kerosene and grease,then kerosene and grease are in
solution:
Goods are in joint supply when they are produced together from the same source, so that increasing the output of one automatically increases the output of the other.

Crude oil refining produces kerosene, grease, petrol and other products together. When the price of crude oil rises, the prices of all these joint products tend to rise, so kerosene and grease are in joint supply.

question: If in the short-run commodity X and commodity Y are supplied jointly, which of the following is correct?

option.a: An increase in demand for Y will raise the price of X
option.b: An increase in demand for X will cause less of Y to be produced
option.c: an increase in demand for X will increase supply of Y
option.d: An increase in demand of X will leave the supply of Y unchanged

solution:
When X and Y are supplied jointly, they come from the same production process. An increase in the demand for X raises its price, so producers increase output of X — and in doing so they automatically produce more of Y as well.

Therefore an increase in demand for X will increase the supply of Y. It does not reduce Y's output or leave it unchanged.

question: If the last Naira spent on each commodity by a consumer gave him equal satisfaction, it means the consumer has been able to
solution:
A consumer maximises satisfaction when the marginal utility per naira spent is equal for every commodity. If the last naira spent on each good gives the same satisfaction, the consumer cannot gain by switching spending from one good to another.

This is the equi-marginal principle, and it describes utility maximisation, not cost or profit maximisation.

question: In a free market economy, resources are allocated through the
solution:
In a free market economy, there is no central planner deciding what to produce. Prices, driven by demand and supply, signal to producers what consumers want and allocate resources through the price mechanism.

State planning committees and government departments belong to a planned economy, and trade unions do not allocate resources.

question: In calculating the Gross National Product (GNP) by the income approach, all the following are included except

option.a: direct taxes paid by persons and companies

solution:
Under the income approach, national income is the sum of incomes earned from production: wages and salaries, rents, interest and profits. Retirement benefits (pensions) are transfer payments — money paid to people without any good or service being produced in return — so they are excluded to avoid double counting.

Direct taxes paid by persons and companies are part of the income earned before tax, so they are included in the incomes (wages and profits) that make up GNP.

question: In determining the growth of a country's population, infant mortality is a component of
solution:
Infant mortality is the number of babies who die before their first birthday. It is therefore a component of the death rate, because it counts deaths in the population.

It is not part of migration, fertility (births) or immigration.

question: Land as a factor of production is made useful through the
solution:
Land in economics means all natural resources. On its own, land produces very little; it becomes useful when human effort is applied to it — clearing, planting, building or mining.

Fertiliser and machines are capital, and “acts of nature” do not by themselves make land productive for human use.
category: Factors of Production and their Theories

question: Malthus' contention is that

option.a: population and food growth rate will, in future, be at par
option.b: population increased in geometric progression while food production increased in arithmetic progression
option.c: nations have to get enough manpower to cultivate available land for food
option.d: population increase in arithmetic progression while food production increased in geometric progression

solution:
Thomas Malthus argued that population grows in geometric progression (1, 2, 4, 8, 16...) while food production grows in arithmetic progression (1, 2, 3, 4, 5...). Population would therefore outrun food supply unless checked.

The other options reverse the two progressions or misstate his argument.

question: Monopoly can best be described as a market in which

option.a: A single seller sells a product which has no close substitute
option.b: The entry of other firms is restricted by the few firms in the market
option.c: Two or more sellers sell a product which is differentiated
option.d: Few sellers sell a product s at different prices

solution:
A monopoly is a market in which a single seller supplies a product that has no close substitute, and new firms are prevented from entering. The monopolist therefore has significant control over price.

Few firms describe an oligopoly, differentiated products describe monopolistic competition, and a single buyer is a monopsony.

question: Net migration is the difference between
solution:
Net migration is the difference between the number of immigrants (people entering a country) and emigrants (people leaving it):

Net migration=Immigrants−Emigrants

If more people enter than leave, net migration is positive; if more leave, it is negative.

question: One advantage of a sole proprietorship is that

option.a: it makes an increase in the volume of business possible
option.b: it can be managed without conflicts
option.c: the sole proprietor raises money from the public
option.d: there is no limit to the number of people who may bring in capital

solution:
A sole proprietorship is owned and run by one person. Because the owner makes all the decisions, there are no partners or shareholders to disagree with, so it can be managed without conflicts.

It cannot raise capital from the public, and its growth is limited by the owner's own resources, so the other options are not advantages of this business form.

question: One disadvantage of direct taxes is that they
solution:
Direct taxes are levied on income and property, such as personal income tax and company tax. One disadvantage is that they can be evaded: people may hide income, fail to declare earnings or under-report profits.

Being progressive is usually seen as an advantage, and allocating scarce resources is not a feature of direct taxes.

question: One disadvantage of inflation is that?
solution:
Inflation hurts people whose incomes are fixed, such as pensioners and workers on fixed salaries. Their money income stays the same while prices rise, so they can buy less and their real income falls.

Businessmen may gain if prices rise faster than costs, and fixed-income earners certainly do not gain.

question: One of the advantages of capitalism is that

option.a: efficient allocation of resources is assured

solution:
In capitalism, private ownership and competition create incentives to produce what consumers want at the lowest cost. Prices act as signals, so resources tend to move to their most profitable uses, giving efficient allocation of resources.

Capitalism encourages private initiative and does not guarantee job security; consumer exploitation is a criticism, not an advantage.

question: One of the factors affecting geographical distribution of population is

option.a: encouragement of early marriages in rural areas
option.b: climatic conditions of the different part of the country

solution:
The geographical distribution of population is influenced by climatic conditions. People tend to settle in areas with favourable climate, fertile land and water, and avoid extremely hot, cold or dry regions.

Early marriage, birth rate and death rate affect population size or growth, not where people are distributed across the country.

question: One relationship between marginal utility and total utility is that when total utility is
solution:
The relationship between total utility (TU) and marginal utility (MU) is that MU is the change in TU. When TU is falling, each extra unit is actually reducing satisfaction, so MU is negative.

When TU is maximum, MU is zero (not maximum). While TU is rising, MU is positive but falling.

question: Population growth rate can be calculated as

option.a: birth rate- death rate + immigrants - emigrants

solution:
The population growth rate takes natural increase and migration into account:

Growth rate=Birth rate−Death rate+Immigrants−Emigrants

Births add to the population, deaths reduce it, immigrants add to it and emigrants leave it. Option C gives only the natural growth rate, not the total growth rate.

question: Small firms are important for the development of a country because

option.a: they render personalized services to the consumers
option.b: they usually produce goods for the elite
option.c: they do not normally provide after sales services
option.d: the prices of their products are usually high

solution:
Small firms are important because they can offer personalised services: they know their customers, respond quickly to special requests and provide goods and services in small, local markets that large firms may ignore.

Producing only for the elite, not providing after-sales service and charging high prices are not reasons why small firms help development.

question: Which of the following is true about the supply of land? It

option.b: is higher in urban than rural areas

solution:
The supply of land is fixed. Land is a free gift of nature, and its total quantity cannot be increased by human effort, even though its quality can be improved.

Its supply does not vary with time, rise with demand or differ in total quantity between town and country; only its use and price change.
category: Factors of Production and their Theories

question: The balance of trade is

option.a: an annual statement showing transaction within a country
option.b: the relationship between a country's receipt from visible and invisible trade
option.c: an account that shows a country's payment to other countries
option.d: the relationship between a country's visible exports and imports

solution:
The balance of trade is the relationship between a country's visible exports and visible imports — that is, trade in physical goods. If visible exports exceed visible imports, there is a trade surplus.

The balance of payments is wider because it includes invisible items and financial flows.

question: The charging of different prices to different groups of buyers for the same goods or services is called?
solution:
Price discrimination is the practice of charging different prices to different groups of buyers for the same good or service, even though the cost of supplying them is the same.

It is common in markets with some monopoly power, such as airlines, cinemas and electricity supply. Monopolistic competition, monopoly and price determination are market structures or processes, not this pricing practice.

question: One of the major factors militating against industrialization in Nigeria is the

option.d: failure to get foreign partners and supporters

solution:
Industrialisation in Nigeria is held back mainly by the inadequacy of infrastructural facilities — unreliable electricity, poor roads, water and transport. Firms must provide these themselves, which raises their costs and makes them less competitive.

Government participation has existed through public enterprises, and foreign partners are not essential for every industry, so infrastructure is the major obstacle.

question: As a country gets more developed, the percentage of labour engaged in agriculture tends to
solution:
As a country develops, the percentage of labour engaged in agriculture decreases steadily. Farms become more mechanised, so fewer workers are needed, while jobs grow in manufacturing and services. This shift is called structural transformation.

It does not remain constant or rise steadily; workers move out of farming, not into it.

question: Given perfect competition in the capital market, the opportunity cost of capital is adequately reflected by the
solution:
Capital is not free: the money used to buy machines could have been lent out to earn interest. Under perfect competition in the capital market, the interest rate is the price of using capital, so it measures the opportunity cost of capital.

Returns on capital are the gain from using it, not its cost, and the shadow price of foreign exchange is a different concept.
category: Factors of Production and their Theories

question: The size of a business unit tends to be small if the activity

option.d: Involves the provision of direct services

solution:
A business unit tends to be small when its activity involves the provision of direct personal services — for example a barber, tailor or repairer. Such services must be delivered personally and cannot easily be mass-produced or expanded without losing quality.

Division of labour, large capital and mass production all encourage large-scale units instead.

question: One of the purpose of advertisement in marketing is to

option.a: Raise the quantity of the product demanded as its price falls
option.b: Shifts the demand curve for the product to the right
option.d: Change the quality of the product

solution:
Advertising informs consumers and changes their tastes in favour of the product. At every price, consumers now want to buy more, so the demand curve shifts to the right.

It does not work by changing the quantity demanded as price falls (that is a movement along the curve), and it does not change the physical quality of the product.

question: When the demand for a good increases owing to an increase in income, it mean that

option.b: there is an increase in quantity demanded
option.c: there is an increase in demand

solution:
When people buy more of a good because their income has risen, the whole demand curve shifts to the right. This is an increase in demand.

An increase in quantity demanded, by contrast, is caused by a fall in the good's own price and is shown by a movement along the same demand curve.

question: The types, sources and uses of government income are mainly concerned with
solution:
Public finance is the branch of economics that studies the types, sources and uses of government income and expenditure, together with public borrowing and debt. It covers taxation, revenue and spending.

Public revenue and public expenditure are only parts of public finance, and the budget is the plan that sets them out.

question: If the cost of production for a firm continues to increase as its output rises, the firm is said to be experiencing
solution:
When a firm's cost of production keeps rising as output increases, it is suffering from diseconomies of scale. The firm has grown beyond its optimum size, and problems of coordination, communication and management push average cost up.

Economies of scale would lower average cost as output rises, and profit maximisation or large-scale production do not describe rising costs.

question: In a free market economy, available resources are more efficiency allocated by complete reliance on
solution:
In a free market economy, there is no central planner. The price system (price mechanism) decides how resources are allocated: rising prices attract resources into an activity and falling prices drive them out.

Strategic planning, development planning and capital budgeting are tools of government direction, not of a free market.

question: The major purpose of African Development Bank is to

option.a: educate peasant farmers in new techniques
option.d: provide loans for development banks in distress

solution:
The African Development Bank (AfDB) provides loans and technical assistance for infrastructural development — roads, power, water, transport and other projects — to promote economic and social development across Africa.

It is not mainly an organisation for teaching farmers, financing ordinary trade, or rescuing distressed banks.

question: The merging of firms engaged in different stages of production and marketing is called
solution:
Vertical integration is the merging of firms that operate at different stages of production and marketing — for example, a firm that produces raw materials joining with one that processes or sells the finished product.

Horizontal integration joins firms at the same stage, while economic union and external economies of scale are unrelated concepts.

question: The co-operatives as a form of business organization differs from partnership by having

option.a: Several sources of capital for business financing
option.b: Ability to issue preferred stocks to members
option.d: Entrenched democratic control in the conduct of business

solution:
A co-operative society is owned and controlled by its members on democratic principles: each member normally has one vote, regardless of how much capital he or she contributed. This democratic control is what distinguishes it from a partnership, where control depends on the partners' agreement.

Both can raise capital from several sources and have rules, so those are not the distinguishing feature.

question: Efficiency in production involves

option.a: Increasing the quantity of the fixed factor of production
option.b: Reducing the size of the work force
option.c: Adopting the quantity of the fixed factors of production
option.d: Producing a given output with the lowest cost combination of factors of production

solution:
Efficiency in production means producing a given output using the lowest-cost combination of factors of production. The firm avoids waste and chooses the cheapest suitable method.

Adding more fixed factors, reducing the workforce or adopting capital-intensive methods does not by itself guarantee efficiency.

question: For a purely competitive industry, a fundamental requirement of the demand curve faced by individual firms is that it should be
solution:
A firm in a purely competitive industry is a price taker: it can sell any quantity at the market price but nothing above it. The demand curve it faces is therefore horizontal, meaning demand is perfectly price elastic.

It is not downward sloping, because the firm cannot influence price, and not perfectly inelastic, because buyers will buy any amount at the market price.

question:
What is the elasticity of demand for commodity X, if at a price of #25 the quantity demanded is 80 and when the price is
reduced to #20 the quantity demanded is 100?
solution:
Use the elasticity formula:

Ed=% change in quantity% change in price

Quantity rises from 80 to 100, a change of 20: 2080×100=25%.

Price falls from ₦25 to ₦20, a change of ₦5: 525×100=20%.

Therefore Ed=2520=1.25.

question: The major determinant of cross elasticity of demand is the

option.d: degree of the necessity of the good

solution:
Cross elasticity measures how the demand for one good responds to a change in the price of another. Its size depends mainly on how close the two goods are as substitutes: close substitutes have a large positive cross elasticity, while unrelated goods have a cross elasticity near zero.

Income, the good's own price and necessity affect demand, but they are not the main determinant of cross elasticity.

question: A firm's Total Revenue (TR) is ₦180,000, while its Total Cost (TC) is #135,000. What is the firm's profit?
solution:
Profit is total revenue minus total cost:

Profit=180{,}000−135{,}000=45{,}000

So the firm's profit is ₦45,000.

question: What to produce in any society is determined by the

option.a: expenditure of the people on different commodities
option.d: supply and demand in the factor markets.

solution:
In a market economy, what to produce is decided by consumers' spending. The goods and services on which people spend most are the ones producers supply, because those sales are profitable.

Competition among producers or consumers and conditions in factor markets influence prices, but the pattern of consumer expenditure is the basic signal of what society wants.

question: Which type of business organization has the attribute of effectively combining management with control?
solution:
A sole proprietorship best combines management with control. The owner provides the capital, makes the decisions and supervises the business, so ownership, management and control are in the same hands.

In a company, ownership is separated from management; in a partnership, control is shared; and in a co-operative, control is democratic but management is usually delegated.

question: The range is used to

option.a: measure the difference between the mean and the mode
option.b: determine the spread of a set of data
option.d: estimate the mean from grouped data

solution:
The range is the difference between the highest and lowest values in a set of data. It is a simple measure of spread or dispersion: a large range means the values are widely spread out.

It is not used to compare the mean and mode, calculate the standard deviation, or estimate the mean from grouped data.
category: Methods and Tools of Economic Analysis

question: A shift in the production possibility frontier could result from

option.d: changes in the combination of goods produced

solution:
The production possibility frontier shows the maximum output an economy can produce with its resources and technology. It shifts outward when the economy's capacity grows.

Changes in production techniques (better technology) increase capacity and shift the frontier outward. Inflation, unemployment and a different combination of goods move the economy along or inside the existing frontier; they do not shift it.

question: The present privatization policy in Nigeria is aimed at

option.c: reducing the prices of goods and services

solution:
Privatisation transfers public enterprises to private owners. Private firms face competition and must control costs, so the main aim is to increase efficiency in production and reduce the burden on government.

Poverty alleviation, reducing inequality and lowering prices may be hoped-for results, but they are not the primary aim of privatisation.

question: Both in the short run and in the long run, a firm maximizes its profits when
solution:
Both in the short run and in the long run, a firm maximises profit at the output where marginal cost equals marginal revenue (MC=MR). Producing one more unit adds the same to revenue as to cost at that point.

Equalities involving average variable cost or average cost do not identify the profit-maximising output.

question: In order to increase its profit margin, the monopolist can manipulate
solution:
A monopolist cannot control both price and quantity at the same time. If it sets a high price, buyers choose a smaller quantity; if it wants to sell more, it must lower the price.

So the monopolist can manipulate either price or output, and the market determines the other.

question: The need to construct a scale of preference is necessitated by

option.a: Scarcity and the need for choice

solution:
A scale of preference is a list of wants arranged in order of importance. It is needed because of scarcity and the need for choice: since a consumer cannot satisfy every want, he or she must rank them and satisfy the most important first.

The need to satisfy wants and the scarcity of resources are related, but the full reason for the scale is scarcity together with choice.

question: The Malthusian theory of population has been rendered ineffective by
solution:
Malthus predicted that population would outrun food supply. His theory has been weakened by technical progress: better seeds, fertilisers, irrigation and machinery have greatly increased food production, so food output has kept pace with population.

Birth control helps, but the main force that proved Malthus wrong is technological improvement in agriculture.

question: Which of the following is an important function of the retailer?

option.c: Breaks bulk and sells products in small units
option.d: Generates demand for products through advertisement

solution:
The retailer is the last link before the consumer. One of the most important functions of the retailer is to break bulk: buy in larger quantities from wholesalers and sell in small units that consumers can afford.

Retailers do not normally grant credit to wholesalers, and reducing distribution cost or advertising are secondary functions.

question:
If y represents the income earned by workers in a factory, find the range of their income which satisfies the following inequality:
4y -300>500.
solution:
Solve the inequality step by step:

4y−300>500

4y>800

y>200

So the workers' income must be greater than 200.

question: If X represents the factors of production and Y represents the factor price, which of the following sets of association is correct?
solution:
Each factor of production has its own reward: land earns rent, capital earns interest, labour earns wages and the entrepreneur earns profit.

Only option B matches all four correctly. The others mix up the rewards, such as giving wages to land or profit to labour.
category: Factors of Production and their Theories

question: A commodity is described as inferior when the
solution:
An inferior good is one whose demand falls when consumers' income rises, because people switch to better substitutes. Its income effect is negative.

The substitution effect is normally positive (a fall in price makes the good relatively cheaper), so it is the income effect that identifies an inferior good.

question: In order to maximize his profit, a businessman who faces a very elastic demand for his products is advised to

option.a: slightly reduce the price of his products
option.b: slightly increase the price of his products

solution:
When demand is very elastic, a small fall in price leads to a large increase in the quantity sold. Total revenue rises because the extra sales more than make up for the lower price per unit.

Raising the price would drive many buyers away and reduce revenue. Price discrimination is not the general advice for a competitive seller facing elastic demand.

question: If at 10k per kg, 1000kg of yam were purchased and at 5k per kg, 1500kg were purchased, the resultant point elasticity of demand is
solution:
Use the point elasticity formula:

Ed=% change in quantity% change in price

Quantity rises from 1000 kg to 1500 kg, a change of 500: 5001000×100=50%.

Price falls from 10k to 5k, a change of 5k: 510×100=50%.

Therefore Ed=5050=1. Demand is unit elastic.

question: In its simplified form, the circular flow of income concept refers to the

option.a: Monetary payments for goods and services produced by individual firms
option.b: Money flows associated with transactions between individual firms and households
option.c: Real flow in goods and services between the product and factor markets
option.d: Transactions in goods and services and payments for such transactions between individual firms and households

solution:
The circular flow of income describes the continuous movement of money, goods and services between households and firms. Households supply factors of production and receive income, then spend that income on goods and services produced by firms.

The full circular flow also includes government and the foreign sector, but in its simplified form it is the two-way flow between households and firms.

question: One of the problems arising from the localization of industries is
solution:
Localisation of industries concentrates industries in one area. Other regions lose investment and jobs, so structural unemployment arises there: the skills and jobs available no longer match the people who need work.

Exportation of output, scarcity of foreign exchange and high prices may occur for other reasons, but structural unemployment is the recognised problem of localisation.

question: An economic system in which the producer and the consumer are the same is referred to as a
solution:
A subsistence economy is one in which people produce mainly for their own consumption: the producer and the consumer are largely the same person or family. Very little is produced for sale or exchange.

In mixed, socialist and capitalist economies, production is mainly for the market, so the producer and consumer are different.

question: The survival of a partnership depends on

option.a: the managerial ability of the partners

solution:
A partnership is not a separate legal person in the same way as a company, and the partners are personally liable for its debts. Its survival therefore depends heavily on mutual trust and the goodwill of the partners; if they quarrel or one withdraws, the partnership may dissolve.

Managerial ability and access to finance matter, but goodwill is the relationship that holds the partnership together.

question:
A student in obu'pu secondary school discovers that he simultaneously needs a biro, an exercise book, an eraser and a ruler, but
that he can purchase only one of these items. What is the first thing he is expected to do?

option.a: draw up a scale of preference
option.b: check how much money he has
option.c: weigh the opportunity cost of each item against the others
option.d: find out which is the cheapest of the items

solution:
The student has several needs but can buy only one item. The first rational step is to draw up a scale of preference, ranking the items from the most to the least important.

Only after ranking can he compare prices, check his money and weigh the opportunity cost of each choice.

question: The advantages which firms obtain directly from expanding their operations are reffered to as
solution:
Internal economies of scale are the advantages a firm obtains directly from expanding its own operations — for example, buying in bulk, using specialised machinery and employing specialist managers.

External economies come from the growth of the whole industry, economies of resource allocation are a market effect, and economies of localisation come from firms clustering together.

solution:

Therefore Ed=66.7300≈0.22. Demand is inelastic.

solution:

question: Which of the following causes the demand curve to shift to the right?

option.a: a reduction in size of population
option.b: an increase in the income of the buyer
option.d: a decrease in price of goods

solution:
This question is about the law of demand.

The correct answer is B: an increase in the income of the buyer. When price changes, the quantity demanded moves in the opposite direction — if price goes up, people buy less; if price goes down, people buy more.

  • A: a reduction in size of population

solution:

solution:
